title: Iff-split of IMO 1986 Q5: IsGood f iff f = fun x => 2 / (2 - x)
intent: Split the characterisation IsGood f ↔ f = fun x ↦ 2 / (2 - x) into its two directions with refine ⟨·, ·⟩. The forward direction is extensionality applied to the already-proved pointwise lemma map_eq; the reverse unfolds the candidate function into the three fields of IsGood with constructor.

applicability.goal_shape: A goal of the form P ↔ Q where P is a characterisation predicate and Q an explicit equation. Here IsGood f ↔ f = fun x ↦ 2 / (2 - x), with IsGood a Prop-valued structure (lines 37-40).
applicability.use_when: the two directions want different tools: one direction is a pointwise equality proved by extensionality of an existing lemma, the other is showing a candidate satisfies each field of a structure, which constructor splits into named cases.
applicability.avoid_when: one direction is definitional or symmetric; both directions need the same rewriting (a single rw/calc chain proves both); or the predicate side is not a structure, so constructor cannot split it into named fields.

claims.claim: The iff goal is split on line 75 by refine ⟨fun hf ↦ funext hf.map_eq, ?_⟩ into exactly two directions, and both close: the forward by funext hf.map_eq, the reverse by the ?_ hole over lines 76-89.

In the reverse direction, constructor (line 77) splits IsGood (fun x ↦ 2 / (2 - x)) into the three fields of IsGood (lines 37-40), each discharged as a separate named case: map_two by simp [tsub_self] (line 78), map_ne_zero by intro x hx; simpa [tsub_eq_zero_iff_le] (line 79), map_add_rev by cases lt_or_ge y 2 with both branches closed (lines 80-89).

The forward direction introduces no new pointwise argument: funext hf.map_eq applies the pointwise lemma map_eq (lines 67-70), so the iff proof reuses the already-proved fact f x = 2 / (2 - x) rather than re-deriving it.

The module docstring states the plan verbatim: 'We formalize the assumptions on f in Imo1986Q5.IsGood predicate, then prove Imo1986Q5.IsGood f ↔ f = fun x ↦ 2 / (2 - x)' (lines 20-21), and the formal proof follows it.

The same iff-split by refine ⟨·, ·⟩ is used in the same file at lines 50-53 for f x = 0 ↔ 2 ≤ x, whose forward direction is not_lt.1 fun hlt ↦ hf.map_ne_zero x hlt hx₀ and reverse is closed by rcases exists_add_of_le hle plus a rewrite.

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 74-89 of the copied file; forward = line 75; reverse = lines 76-89; children = the two goals created by refine ⟨·, ·⟩; structure_fields = fields of the IsGood structure (lines 37-40)

consequences: refine ⟨·, ·⟩ on an iff creates exactly two obligations — the forward and reverse implication — each to be closed on its own. The reverse direction here is not self-contained: constructor further splits it into the three fields of IsGood, so the reverse child is far larger than the forward (14 lines versus 1). Failure mode: the forward direction silently leans on an earlier pointwise lemma (map_eq), so the iff itself looks near-trivial while the real work happened earlier in the file; anyone reproducing the whole argument must also carry the upstream lemmas (map_of_lt_two, map_eq_zero, lines 50-70).
